subject: Cloud Computing
title: Google Cloud's 2019 Networking Failure
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Google Cloud's 2019 Networking Failure.

hook.text: In June 2019, Google Cloud went down for 4.5 hours. YouTube, Gmail, Snapchat, and Discord all went dark.

buildup.text: A network configuration change meant to apply to a few servers was accidentally applied to an entire region.

discovery.text: The misconfiguration caused network congestion that cascaded. Services fought for bandwidth and choked each other.

twist.text: Google's internal tools were also affected. Engineers had to work around their own broken systems to fix the problem.

climax.text: Google published a detailed post-mortem explaining exactly what happened. Transparency after failure builds trust.

punchline.text: Even Google breaks. The fix tool was broken too.

quiz.question: What made the 2019 Google Cloud outage especially hard to fix?
options: Google's own internal repair tools were affected by the same failure
The outage was caused by a natural disaster
Google didn't have any engineers on duty that day

details.summary: In June 2019, a Google Cloud networking configuration change caused widespread outages affecting Google Cloud, YouTube, Gmail, and Snapchat for over four hours. The incident impacted multiple regions simultaneously, violating customer expectations of regional independence.
details.whyItMatters: Google's network is considered among the best in the world. This failure proved that even elite infrastructure teams make configuration mistakes with global cascading consequences.
takeaways: A configuration change caused multi-region network failures
Google Cloud, YouTube, and Gmail all went down simultaneously
Network changes can have blast radius beyond a single region

faq.question: What caused the Google Cloud networking failure?
faq.answer: A configuration change intended for a small set of servers was mistakenly applied broadly, causing network congestion that cascaded across regions. The error overloaded network capacity in multiple locations simultaneously, degrading services globally.

faq.question: What did Google change after the incident?
faq.answer: Google improved configuration change validation, added canary deployment for network changes, enhanced monitoring for early detection of cascading failures, and committed to faster customer communication during incidents.
